Sodium content DERIVED, not measured: 22.99/58.44 = 39.339% of pure NaCl by mass, x 100 g = 39339 mg. Corrected 2026-07-31 from 38758, which was a measured table-salt value (implying ~98.5% NaCl purity) sitting under a note that claimed the stoichiometric derivation -- the number and its stated justification did not match. The derivation is chosen over the measured value for reproducibility: anyone can rederive it from two atomic masses, whereas the measured figure needs a source document nobody here has opened. NOTE THE COST: iodised table salt is NOT pure NaCl (anti-caking agents, potassium iodate, moisture), so this figure describes the derivation and overstates a real product's sodium by roughly 1.5%. It is a reproducible upper bound, not a product measurement. verified=false: no primary source has been opened for either figure

Hand-entered approximation; no primary source opened. DIAAS 1.00 is AUTHORED, not sourced: dairy casein is recalled from the DIAAS literature as scoring at or above 1.0 (milk protein concentrate is usually quoted near 1.1-1.2), and 1.00 is entered as the low end of that recollection rather than the midpoint, because a high DIAAS is what makes a row QUALIFY under the quality-source rule and the cheapest authoring path must not produce the most permissive output. Nobody has opened FAO 2013 or any DIAAS primary source in this build. See docs/methodology.md, 'DIAAS values are authored, and the quality rule turns on them'

Hand-entered approximation; no primary source opened. DIAAS 0.65 is AUTHORED, not sourced, and the recollection behind it is WIDE: published figures for soy foods recalled anywhere between roughly 0.5 for tofu and 0.9 for soy protein isolate, the spread depending on processing and on which reference amino-acid pattern was used. 0.65 sits near the low end of that spread, entered conservatively for the reason given on paneer_fresh. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE, which is not hidden: 0.65 falls BELOW the 0.75 quality threshold, so tofu does not qualify as a high-quality protein source in this system. That is a data-confidence outcome, not a nutritional finding about tofu. See docs/methodology.md
